rejected.title: Polymers and plastics
card: A polymer is a very long molecule made of many small molecules joined in a repeating chain. The small repeating molecule is called a monomer.
Many polymers, including most plastics, are made from crude oil, which is a finite resource. Polyethylene, used in shopping bags, is one example.
Many plastics break down very slowly. They can last for centuries in the environment, where they can harm wildlife and build up as waste.
Because of this, alternatives are being developed, such as plastics made from plant material and plastics designed to break down faster.
rejected.remember: Many polymers, including most plastics, are made from crude oil, and many plastics can last for centuries as waste.

a.q: Which statement best describes a polymer?
opts: A long molecule made of many small molecules in a chain
A single large atom made of many smaller atoms joined
A mixture of different plastics melted into one block
A small molecule that is the starting unit of a plastic
a.why: A polymer is a long chain of repeating small molecules. The last option describes a monomer, which is one unit of the chain, not the whole chain.
a.clue: Think of a chain made of many identical links.

b.q: Dev's council wants to cut plastic waste in a local creek. Which reason best explains why plastic bags left near the creek are a long-term problem?
opts: Many plastics break down so slowly they can last centuries
Plastics come from crude oil, so they dissolve in water
Plastics are made of monomers, which poison all animals
Plastics are finite, so the creek will soon run out of them
b.why: Many plastics break down very slowly, so a bag left near the creek can remain for centuries. Being made from crude oil does not make plastic dissolve in water, and the finite supply of oil is a separate issue from how long waste lasts.
b.clue: Focus on what happens to plastic after it is thrown away.

a.q: Which statement best describes a polymer?
opts: A long chain of many small molecules joined together
One small molecule that repeats to form a long chain
A single giant atom built from many smaller atoms
A mixture of plastics melted together into one block
a.why: A polymer is the whole long chain, made of many small repeating molecules. The second option describes a monomer, which is one unit of the chain, not the whole chain.
a.clue: Is a polymer the whole structure or one of its parts?

b.q: Dev's council wants to cut plastic waste in a local creek. Why are plastic bags left near the creek a long-term problem?
opts: They can stay in the creek for hundreds of years
They can dissolve into the water within a few weeks
They can turn back into crude oil as they break down
They can rot in months and add nutrients to the soil
b.why: Plastic bags break down very slowly, so one left by the creek can stay there for centuries, harming wildlife and building up as waste. They do not dissolve or rot away within weeks or months, and breaking down does not turn them back into crude oil.
b.clue: Think about how fast plastic breaks down once it is thrown away.
